title: Session Warmth Index and Dashboard Proposal
summary: Proposal for a compact, actionable "Session Warmth Index" (SWI) plus a lightweight dashboard and trace annotations to make cold-start/cold-cache behavior visible across multi-tenant LLM serving. Focus: operator-facing SLI, product-facing UX impact signals, and cost attribution for cold sessions.
goals: Define a single composite metric (Session Warmth Index) that correlates with first-response latency and token cost
Provide a small set of dashboard widgets to help oncall and SRE triage cold-session incidents quickly
Standardize trace annotations and span tags to reconstruct session warming lifecycle end-to-end
Enable chargeback/cost attribution for cold versus warm sessions in Dedicated/Hosted tiers
motivation_and_context: We see recurring incidents where high 95th/99th p(latency) changes are driven by a small fraction of cold sessions (client opens rarely used model/tenant or long idle period). Existing dashboards show token-level latencies but not an aggregated session-level view. This proposal is intended to sit alongside the existing latency SLO work but provide a higher-signal, lower-cardinality SLI for operators and product owners.
session_warmth_index_definition:
SWI = weighted_avg([kv_cache_hit_rate, model_warm_flag, avg_first_token_latency_bucket_score, recent_activity_score]) mapped to 0..100 where higher = warmer. Components:
- kv_cache_hit_rate: percent of requests in session that hit KV (0..1) scaled 0..50 points
- model_warm_flag: boolean (1 if model instance warmed in last 30s) mapped to 0/30 points
- avg_first_token_latency_bucket_score: bucket 0 (<40ms)->30, 1(40-150ms)->20, 2(150-500ms)->10, 3(>500ms)->0 (normalized)
- recent_activity_score: session requests per minute in last 5 min normalized to 0..20 points
Example: session with kv_hit=0.9 (45), warmed=1 (30), latency_bucket=1 (20), activity=0.5 (10) -> SWI=105 capped to 100 -> treated as hot. Adjust weights in rollout phase.
metric_definitions_and_labels:
All metrics should be emitted with the following labels: tenant_id, route, model_name, model_variant, instance_id, deploy_region, session_id (if available), is_dedicated. Key metrics to instrument:
- swi.value: numeric 0..100 (gauge) emitted at session end and periodic heartbeat every 30s (labels above)
- kv.cache.hits / kv.cache.misses (counters) with session_id and token_index
- inference.first_token.latency_ms (histogram) with session_id, request_id, model_variant
- model.instance.warm_timestamp (gauge unix_ts) per instance_id
- session.activity.count (counter) per session_id (increments per request)
- swi.source_notes (string tag) optional for debugging (e.g., "kv-dominant", "cold-model")
alerting_and_slos:
Suggested SLI: percentage of sessions with SWI <= 20 in the 28-day rolling window mapped to a product-level SLO for 99th percentile latency. Example alerting rules:
- P50/P95/P99 of swi.value by tenant > threshold (e.g., P99 SWI < 20) -> Sev3
- sudden spike: delta( count(sessions where SWI <= 20) over 15m ) > 5x baseline -> Pager (investigate model warm pool eviction)
trace_and_span_guidelines:
Span names and tags to add for reconstructing warmth lifecycle:
- span: session.bootstrap (start of session/context creation) tags: session_id, user_agent, route
- span: kv.lookup (per request) tags: session_id, cache_key, hit:true/false, shard_id
- span: model.alloc (when a model instance is selected/spun up) tags: instance_id, model_variant, cold_start:true/false, queued_for_launch
- span: model.init (model weights map/quant load) tags: instance_id, loader_duration_ms
- span: inference.decode (per response generation) tags: session_id, tokens_generated, batch_size
- recommended trace-level annotations: "kv_hit_ratio_session", "first_token_latency_ms", "model_warm_age_s"
Sampling guidance: weight traces with first_token_latency_ms > 150ms or kv_hit=false higher to ensure cold-session behaviors sampled more frequently; cap total sample rate to budget (e.g., 1% global, 10% for suspect traces).
dashboard_wireframe_and_widgets:
Target: compact 6-panel dashboard for oncall + 2 product tiles for product teams. Widgets (operator view):
1) Topline: sessions/sec, unique_sessions_5m, %sessions_with_SWI<=20 (timeseries)
2) Heatmap: SWI distribution by tenant (rows) x hour (columns) - quick hotspot detection
3) Trace-linked table: recent low-SWI sessions with link to trace and sample queries (columns: session_id, tenant_id, first_token_p50, kv_hit_rate, model_variant, trace_link)
4) Rollup: cost delta per session (est token-cost) for low vs high SWI (bar chart)
5) Instance warm pool status: count of warmed instances per model_variant, warm_age histogram
6) Canary probe success rate: synthetic probe latency and SWI over last 24h
Product view widgets (2):
- %user-facing slow responses attributable to SWI<=20 (pie)
- session-level conversion / retry rate vs SWI buckets
Placement: small, mobile-friendly layout for quick paging via console.
sample_queries_and_promql: Example SQL (bigquery): SELECT tenant_id, COUNT(1) as sessions, AVG(swi_value) as avg_swi, PERCENTILE_CONT(first_token_latency_ms, 0.95) as p95_first_token FROM telemetry.sessions WHERE _PARTITIONTIME BETWEEN TIMESTAMP_SUB(CURRENT_TIMESTAMP(), INTERVAL 1 DAY) AND CURRENT_TIMESTAMP() GROUP BY tenant_id ORDER BY p95_first_token DESC LIMIT 50;
instrumentation_checklist: Emit swi.value as a gauge from session manager (heartbeat + session end)
Instrument kv.lookup spans with hit/miss and per-token tags
Expose model.instance.warm_timestamp and instance_id metadata in instance host agent
Add first_token latency histogram in inference runtime and tag with session_id
Add session_id propagation across proxy -> router -> runtime -> model process
Ensure synthetic probes (canary) emit SWI so we can compare real vs synthetic
Update telemetry ingestion to retain session-level indices for 14 days (adjustable)
rollout_plan_and_milestones: Phase 0 (experiment, 2 weeks): emit swi.value for 10% of traffic (sampling) for a small set of model_variants; validate distribution and tweak weights
Phase 1 (pilot, 4 weeks): full emission for internal tenants + canary agents; deploy dashboard in read-only mode for SRE
Phase 2 (ops, 6 weeks): enable alerts, integrate with oncall runbooks, add cost attribution link to billing datasets
Phase 3 (product, ongoing): product dashboards, expose SWI to customers in Console with explanation and recommended mitigations
open_questions_and_risks: Weighting: are KV hits or model warm state more predictive of end-to-end latency? Need initial offline correlation study

Cardinality: session_id + tenant + model may create high-cardinality labels—we should avoid emitting high-cardinality labels to metric series; keep session_id only on traces and session-level metrics as ephemeral (not dimension for long-term aggregates)
Privacy: session-level traces may contain PII in prompts — ensure prompt redaction and PHI scrubbing in traces before linking from dashboard
Cost: storing session-level data for 14 days increases ingestion costs; consider a secondary compressed index for low-SWI sessions only
